pretriaged_by: orchestrator, 2026-11-10, before committing an extraction agent
why_pretriaged: The ready queue was empty and this was one of two headlessly fetchable pending papers. Measuring the SI first cost two tool calls and changed the decision.

acquisition.supplements: Europe PMC /PMC11878168/supplementaryFiles -- HTTP 200, 5,367,946 B, magic 504b0304, VALID ZIP, extracted to source/suppl/ (33 files)
acquisition.note: The same route returned HTTP 500 for PMC13450591 and a 297-byte XML stub for PMC11099935, so it is per-PMCID and must be judged by magic bytes AND size together.

si_tables_measured.method: dumped word/document.xml directly rather than trusting a scanner (F-070)
si_tables_measured.table_1: an IL10 mRNA ORF sequence -- not a screen
si_tables_measured.table_2: 5 rows (4 data) | HA to Lipids molar ratio % | Size | Zeta | EE% | Transfection Efficiency % <- THE ONLY DELIVERY READOUT
si_tables_measured.tables_3_to_6: ML outputs and hyperparameter grids -- not measurements

reasoning: The only admissible readout is Transfection Efficiency % in a FOUR-data-row table, and its variable is the HA-to-lipid molar ratio -- a FORMULATION axis, not chemistry. That is F-067's pattern for the eighth time.
Labels (MC3, LNP2, PEG2000, S2) suggest one or two ionizable lipids, both likely benchmarks already in the corpus -- so the chemical support gained is ~0 regardless of row count.
Licence is CC BY-NC. NC fails CLAUDE.md section 8's CC0/CC-BY requirement on its own, so even a clean extraction could not be released with the corpus.
Two agents were already running and the marginal value of a third on ~4 formulation rows of benchmark chemistry is lower than the acquisition and adjudication work left.
what_a_future_session_should_do: If the main text holds a larger per-formulation screen with a translated readout, extract it -- the SI alone does not. The figures are already on disk. Resolve the NC licence question before any release either way.
not_asserted: This is a triage judgement from the SI only. The main-text figures were NOT read, so 'low yield' is a claim about what is on disk, not about the paper.
